(quae sint ea nūmina) · also exclam. adj., n. acc. pl. (quae bella exhausta canebat!; quae … regna) · also interrog. pron./adj., n. acc. pl., what? (quae quibus anteferam; quae … maiora) · also f. nom. pl. (quae … acies)
qualem: quālis, -e — of what kind, such as, as (f. acc. sg.; with obscūram, 'such as one who ... sees the moon')
quantum: quantus, -a, -um — how much, as much as (n. acc./nom. sg.; also adv.)
quas: quī, quae, quod — who, which, what (rel. or interrog., f. acc. pl.)
quem: quī, quae, quod — who, whom (rel. or interrog., m. acc. sg.) · quis, quid after sī, nē — any(one), some(one) (indef., m. acc. sg.: sī quem)
qui: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel. pron., m. nom. sg./pl.) · interrog. adj./pron., who? which? (m. nom. sg./pl.: Sed vos qui tandem) · also exclam. adj., what (youths)! (m. nom. pl.: Quī iuvenēs!)
quibus: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel., abl./dat. pl.) · interrog. adj., what? which? (abl./dat. pl.) · also indef. after sī, any (abl./dat. pl.: sī quibus silvīs)
quidem: quidem (adv.) — indeed, to be sure; at least
quod: quī, quae, quod — which (rel., n. nom./acc. sg.); quod (conj.), because, that · also interrog. adj., what? (n. nom./acc. sg.: quod genus) · also acc. of respect, wherefore (quod tē per superōs … ōrō) · also indef. adj. after sī, any (n. nom. sg.: sī quod nūmen) · also connective, but, now (quod sī, 'but if'; n. acc. sg. as conj.)
quondam: quondam (adv.) — once, formerly, at one time
quos: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel. or interrog., m. acc. pl.) · quis after sī — any(one) (indef., m. acc. pl.: sī quos)
recessit: recēdō, -ere, -cessī, -cessum — to withdraw, stand back, recede (3 sg. perf.)
recipitque: recipiō, -ere, -cēpī, -ceptum — to take back, admit, receive (3rd sg. pres.) + -que, and
reditus: reditus, -ūs (m.) — return, homecoming (nom. pl.) · also acc. pl. (reditūs)
regia: rēgius, -a, -um — royal, queenly (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · also rēgia, -ae (f.), palace, royal house (nom. sg.: rēgia Pīcī)
reliquit: relinquō, -ere, relīquī, relictum — to leave behind, abandon (3rd sg. perf.)
res: rēs, reī (f.) — thing, matter, affair; state (nom. sg.; nom./acc. pl.)
rutulo: Rutulus, -a, -um — Rutulian, of the Rutuli, Turnus's people (m. abl. sg., with sanguine) · also as noun, m. dat. sg., the Rutulian, i.e. Turnus
salve: salveō, -ēre — to be well; salvē, hail, greetings (sg. imper.)
sanguine: sanguis, sanguinis (m.) — blood; descent, lineage (abl. sg.)
sed: sed (conj.) — but; sed enim, but indeed
sedes: sēdēs, sēdis (f.) — seat, abode, settlement (acc./nom. pl.) · also nom. sg. (sēdēs fundātur)
segnes: segnis, -e — slow, sluggish, slack (m. voc. pl., addressing the Trojans)
senior: senior, -ius — older, aged; senior (m.), an elder, old man (comp. of senex, m. nom. sg.)
sequuntur: sequor, sequī, secūtus sum — to follow (3rd pl. pres., deponent)
servabat: servō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to keep, guard, watch over (3rd sg. impf.)
sese: sē, sēsē — emphatic reflexive, himself, itself, themselves (acc.)
seu: seu (sīve) — or if; seu… seu, whether… or
sic: sīc (adv.) — so, thus, in this way
sidera: sīdus, sīderis (n.) — star, constellation; pl. the sky (acc./nom. pl.)
sidonia: Sīdōnius, -a, -um — of Sidon, Phoenician, Carthaginian (f. nom. sg.) · also f. abl. sg. (Sīdōniā urbe, 'from the Sidonian city')
signa: signum, -ī (n.) — sign, portent, token (acc. pl.) · also nom. pl.
solutae: solvō, -ere, solvī, solūtum — to loosen, untie, release (perf. pass. part., f. nom. pl.; also gen./dat. sg.)
sospite: sospes, -itis — safe, unharmed, preserving (m./f./n. abl. sg.)
spolia: spolium, -ī (n.) — spoils, armour stripped from a foe (acc./nom. pl.)
sternitur: sternō, -ere, strāvī, strātum — to lay low, strew, stretch out (3rd sg. pres. pass.)
stipata: stīpō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to press together, crowd round, throng (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg.; also n. nom./acc. pl.)
sua: suus, -a, -um — his, her, its, their own (f. nom./abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
subligat: subligō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to bind on, gird on, tie beneath (3rd sg. pres.)
sublimem: sublīmis, -e — lifted high, aloft (m./f. acc. sg.)
substitit: substō, substāre, substitī — to stand still, stop (3rd sg. perf.)
suis: suus, -a, -um — his/her/its/their own (m./f./n. abl. pl.; also dat. pl.) · sūs, suis — pig (dat./abl. pl., rare)
sunt: sum, esse, fuī — to be; there are; sunt mihi, I have (3rd pl. pres.)
suo: suus, -a, -um — his/her/their own (reflexive poss.) (m./n. abl. sg.)
superbo: superbus, -a, -um — proud, splendid, haughty (m./n. abl./dat. sg.)
superest: supersum, -esse, -fuī — to remain, be left over (3rd sg. pres.)
superi: superus, -a, -um — above, upper; superī (m. pl.), the gods above (gen. sg. m.; nom. pl. m.) · also m. voc. pl. (Superī, address to the gods)
supremum: suprēmus, -a, -um — last, final, uttermost (m. acc. sg.; n. nom./acc. sg.)
surgens: surgō, -ere, surrexī, surrectum — to rise, spring up (pres. part., m. nom. sg.)
suspendit: suspendō, -ere, -pendī, -pensum — to hang up, suspend (3rd sg. pres.)
tardet: tardō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to slow, hinder, delay (3rd sg. pres. subj.)
tegebat: tegō, -ere, tēxī, tēctum — to cover, hide, shelter (3rd sg. impf.)
tela: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, weapon, spear, dart (acc./nom. pl.)
telaque: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, spear, dart, weapon (acc./nom. pl.) + -que, and
telas: tēla, -ae (f.) — web, warp; woven cloth (acc. pl.)
tempus: tempus, -oris (n.) — time, season, hour (nom. sg.) · also n. acc. sg. (tempus inane peto)
tendebat: tendō, -ere, tetendī, tentum — to stretch; direct one's course, hasten (3rd sg. impf.)
tenui: tenuis, -e — thin, slender, fine (m./f./n. abl. sg.; n. dat. sg.)
terrae: terra, -ae (f.) — earth, land, country (gen./dat. sg.; nom. pl.)
teucrique: Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — the Teucrians, Trojans (nom. pl.) + -que, and
thoraca: thōrāx, -ācis (m.) — breastplate, cuirass (acc. sg., Greek form -a)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
tolli: tollō, -ere, sustulī, sublātum — to lift up, carry off, take away (pres. pass. inf.)
tollunt: tollō, -ere, sustulī, sublātum — to lift, raise; se tollere, to rise up (3rd pl. pres.)
toros: torus, -ī (m.) — couch, bed; dining-couch, raised bank (acc. pl.)
tropaeum: tropaeum, -ī (n.) — trophy, victory-memorial (nom./acc. sg., in apposition to arma)
trunca: truncus, -a, -um — lopped, stripped of branches (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
turnus: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, young king of the Rutulians, suitor of Lavinia (nom. sg.)
umectat: ūmectō, -āre — to moisten, wet, bathe (3rd sg. pres.)
unam: ūnus, -a, -um — one, one alone, single (f. acc. sg.)
undique: undique (adv.) — from all sides, on every side
unguibus: unguis, -is (m.) — nail, claw, talon (abl. pl.; also dat. pl.)
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how · also + subj., how (indirect exclamation: cernis ut insultent) · also + subj., oh that (wish: ut … ludar)
vale: valeō, -ēre, -uī — to be well, be strong; valē, farewell (sg. imper.)
vellere: vellō, -ere, vellī (vulsī), vulsum — to pluck, tear up (pres. inf.)
vero: vērō (adv.) — in truth, indeed, but; tum vērō, then indeed
versis: vertō, -ere, vertī, versum — to turn, change (perf. pass. part., m./n. abl./dat. pl.)
videbis: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (2nd sg. fut.)
videres: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (2nd sg. impf. subj.)
vidit: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (3rd sg. perf.)
vimine: vīmen, -inis (n.) — pliant twig, shoot, osier (abl. sg.)
viresque: vīs (f.) — force; pl. vīrēs, strength (acc. pl.) + -que, and
viri: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero, husband (nom. pl.; gen. sg.) · also voc. pl. (festīnāte, virī)
virtutis: virtūs, -ūtis (f.) — manly excellence, valour, courage (gen. sg.)
vocant: vocō, -āre — to call, name, summon (3rd pl. pres.)
vota: vōtum, -ī (n.) — vow, promise to a god, prayer (acc./nom. pl.)
vulnus: vulnus, vulneris (n.) (= volnus) — wound, blow (nom./acc. sg.)
